items.title: Doctors Are from Mars, Nurses Are from Venus
items.summary: To improve patient outcomes, a shared clinical language must validate both the nurse's qualitative insight and the physician's demand for quantitative evidence. Clinical decision support tools can serve as translators, when designed thoughtfully.

items.title: How to Vet Early Warning Scores
items.summary: Vetting early warning scores is not for the faint of heart. Check out our latest blog post to avoid some of the common pitfalls.

items.title: The Ten Commandments for Hospital Rapid Response Teams
items.summary: Hospital rapid response teams (RRTs) provide on-the-fly critical care in respiratory, cardiac, neurologic, and other clinical emergencies. Since RRTs are generally not the primary service, they are often dependent on the willingness of front line providers and nurses to be activated. As such, RRT members are part craftsman, delivering expert care, and part salesperson, encouraging the hospital to use their services. We therefore propose the following Ten Commandments for Hospital Rapid Response Teams to engender strong collaboration and RRT program success.

items.title: Sepsis Alliance Webinar Recap: Sepsis Prediction Models + Yale’s eCART Case Study
items.summary: At a recent Sepsis Alliance webinar, three experts weighed in on why sepsis prediction models are failing us and how we might rethink the current approach to identify patients at risk of sepsis with the fewest false alarms.

items.title: The Undeniable Link Between Sepsis and Clinical Deterioration
items.summary: Sepsis and deterioration are not two different problems but rather one and the same with septic patients at high risk of deterioration and deteriorating patients at high risk of being septic.

items.title: Why Real-World Testing Should be a Must for AI Early Warning Devices
items.summary: Medical AI devices, even when cleared by FDA, often lack real world testing. AgileMD shares why prospective clinical validation should be a must to ensure model generalizability and what they learned from their FDA clearance process of eCART for clinical deterioration prediction.

items.title: eCART FDA Clearance
items.summary: AgileMD receives FDA clearance for eCART to predict in-hospital clinical deterioration across medical conditions In clinical testing, AgileMD’s eCART Clinical DeteriorationSuite accurately identified high-risk hospitalized patients across conditions, including sepsis, heart failure, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
